clue.text: No longer played one's part as demanded

parts.note: a former partner is an ex, someone no longer in the role
an actor who played a part has acted

explanation.surface: An actor retired from the stage after performing exactly as required.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exacted was insisted upon or required from someone.

clue.text: Remove from duty

definitions.meaning: to cut out
a tax charged on goods

explanation.surface: Take something off the list of taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut out is to remove surgically, and a tax on goods like alcohol is a duty.

clue.text: Bureau provides data in current year

indicators.note: the data sit inside the abbreviation for current

parts.note: AC is alternating current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An office supplies figures for this year.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an office or organisation providing a service.

clue.text: Acknowledging acclaim for going on the fiddle

definitions.meaning: bending forward to applause at the end of a show
picking up the stick strung with horsehair to play a violin

explanation.surface: A performer thanks the crowd while fiddling the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers bend in thanks for applause, and a violinist picks up the stick used to play the violin.

clue.text: Money needed for kneading

definitions.meaning: slang for cash
the mix of flour and water that a baker works by hand

explanation.surface: Cash is required to make bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash, and the bread mixture a baker works by hand.

clue.text: Butler in post has a moral tale to tell

indicators.note: the politician's name sits within the word for a post

parts.note: a pale is a wooden stake or fence post
Rab Butler was a British Conservative statesman, so Butler gives RAB

explanation.surface: A household butler stationed at his post has an improving story to recount.
explanation.walkthrough: Butler is not a manservant but R. A. 'Rab' Butler, the post-war Conservative minister; PALE is a stake, as in 'beyond the pale'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short story told to teach a lesson, as in the Gospels, is a moral fable.

clue.text: What pretentious vocalists do?

parts.note: reads as affected behaviour, but singers also present their songs or melodies to an audience

explanation.surface: A question about how showy singers behave.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing off haughtily, and literally staging tunes, since an air is a melody.

clue.text: Bloody uncommon

definitions.meaning: of meat, cooked only briefly so it stays red
seldom found

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is very unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak barely cooked is red inside, and anything seldom seen is unusual.

clue.text: Mistakes made by lingerie manufacturers

definitions.meaning: embarrassing errors
loose knickers produced by underwear makers

explanation.surface: Errors committed by underwear firms.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for blunders, and the baggy knee-length knickers of old.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: to enchant or delight
a door or gate

explanation.surface: Smooth-talk your way through the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant puts someone in a trance, and a door is an access point.

clue.text: The audacity of the chap

definitions.meaning: nerve or impudence, as in 'what a nerve'
chap or chop is an old word for the jaw or side of the face

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how bold a certain man is.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is called lip or nerve, and the old 'chaps' or 'chops' are the jaws and fleshy sides of the face.

clue.text: To speak more than anyone else is extreme

parts.note: to utter is to say or speak
the most is more than anyone else has

explanation.surface: Talking more than everybody else is going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost is a literary synonym for utmost, the furthest or greatest degree.

clue.text: Used to be a timely indicator

definitions.meaning: pre-owned goods are not new
a pointer on a clock face that shows the time

explanation.surface: Something old was once a sign of good timing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-owned car is not new, and the fast-sweeping pointer on a watch counts off seconds.

clue.text: Frenchmen featured in each Austen novel

indicators.note: the Frenchmen appear inside the abbreviation for each

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: French characters appear in every one of Jane Austen's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a matchmaking heroine bears this title.

clue.text: Current way to produce greater efficiency

parts.note: a stream is a flowing current of water
a line is a route or course, as in a railway line

explanation.surface: Using the latest methods to make things run better.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an organisation simpler and more effective by cutting waste.

clue.text: Scottish pair unusually tense

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Two Scots are oddly on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges SCOTTISHPAIR. 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the nervous pair, but it is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The French past historic is a verb tense used for completed actions in written narrative.

clue.text: Will examine people in a short time

parts.note: to test is to examine

indicators.note: the people go inside the pieces for a short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
men are people

explanation.surface: Someone will check on a group of people in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the auxiliary verb but is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Did a nose disorder result from them?

definitions.text: Did a nose disorder result from them?

indicators.note: the three words are thrown into disorder to make a new word

explanation.surface: A question whether some growths caused a nasal complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges DIDANOSE; the whole clue also asks whether a nasal problem came from these growths.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen lymph tissue at the back of the nose can block breathing, a nasal complaint.

clue.text: Added note makes changes to liturgical books

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter
alters means makes changes

explanation.surface: An appended note revises some prayer books.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books of the Psalms used in church worship.

clue.text: Daughter and one son had to be ousted

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
I is the Roman numeral for one
to have something is to possess it

explanation.surface: A family's daughter and one son had to be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dispossessed means being deprived of one's property, evicted.

clue.text: Deliver a blow to the workings of the economy!

definitions.meaning: to hit
a walkout halts the workings of industry, a joking take on industrial action

explanation.surface: A call to strike against how the economy works.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit someone, and a stoppage by workers that brings the economy's workings to a halt.

clue.text: Shrouds for spirits of the dead

definitions.meaning: covers that screen light
ghosts in the underworld

explanation.surface: Burial cloths for ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Screens and blinds cover things, and ghosts of the underworld in classical poetry.

clue.text: Blue and white African flower

parts.note: reads as a two-coloured bloom from Africa, but a flower here is something that flows, a river with Blue and White branches meeting at Khartoum

explanation.surface: A bicoloured bloom from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of north-east Africa forms from its Blue and White tributaries, and a flower is a thing that flows.

clue.text: Arrange a partnership and coordinate

definitions.meaning: to pair two people off, as a matchmaker does
to make things harmonise or go together

explanation.surface: Set up a business partnership and organise it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaker pairs off a couple, and colours or items that harmonise go together.

clue.text: Make a terrine and give him a portion of it

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so a part of the words make a terrine supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Cook a pâté and give a man a slice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a portion of' points at a run of letters within 'Make a terrine'; 'him' is the person given the portion.
explanation.definitionFit: The man given a share of the dish is the person who consumes it, a diner.

clue.text: At liberty to offer the rouble in payment

indicators.note: the currency letter sits in the payment

parts.note: a fee is a payment for services
R is the abbreviation for the rouble

explanation.surface: Free to pay in roubles.
explanation.definitionFit: At liberty means unconfined, not held captive.

clue.text: Anne tries for a change to be serious

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Anne attempts, just this once, to be grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning something sincerely and with determination is being serious about it.

clue.text: Heroic saga of one Irish house overturned

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down-looking sense the Irish chamber's name is turned back to front

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: An epic tale about a single Irish home being knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns DAIL into LIAD, placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is the classic heroic narrative.

clue.text: Mistrust American president circumscribed by nonconformist group

indicators.note: to be circumscribed is to be enclosed within limits, so the first pieces sit inside the group

parts.note: a sect is a breakaway religious group

explanation.surface: Distrust a US leader hemmed in by a dissenting faction.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt someone's honesty is to distrust them.

clue.text: Midshipmen's joints

definitions.meaning: in naval slang junior officers who reefed the sails
cannabis cigarettes

explanation.surface: Young naval officers sharing cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval slang names midshipmen after the sail-shortening duty, and slang also names cannabis cigarettes so.
